lines.text: Every world record is a claim.
Thousands of records, and you have to take each one on trust.
And a claim is only as good as its proof.
Any%: every run is a tiny log anyone can replay.
Change one byte, and the fingerprint breaks.
A speedrun: finish a game as fast as you possibly can.
The fastest time on the board is the world record.
And the only thing standing behind it is a video.
Splice two attempts together, and the video looks like one run.
Mod the game to change the odds, and the video still looks fair.
Or slow the game down, and play the video back at full speed.
Video can't tell which. So we stopped trusting video.
This is Any%: a handheld console, built for speedrunning.
Fifty-nine parts, from the shell to the screws.
A five-inch touchscreen, and a Raspberry Pi to run the games.
Our own games, with fixed rules: same inputs in, same run out.
The buttons are cosmetic for now: pair a controller, and play.
And every input, every frame, is written to a log.
Ship It: run the hackathon office.
Rush Hour: Mumbai's trains, against the clock.
Zip: a packet racing through the venue.
Marine Drive GP: three laps, three rivals.
Segfault: bugs in the server room.
Five games. Any run in any of them can be checked, by anyone.
A full run of Rush Hour, logged by the game itself.
Every button, every frame, written down as it is played.
The whole run, every frame of it, fits in 731 bytes.
Hand that log to anyone. They replay it, with the same rules.
The fingerprints match: the run is exactly what those inputs produce.
Now change a single bit of the log. Byte 381.
The fingerprint changes. A modded game fails too; a spliced log desyncs.
The real checker, run on a laptop, with its actual output.
Five games, five run logs. Each one checked in milliseconds.
The same log also coaches you. Meet PB, the launcher's coach.
It replays both runs, and finds where the time went.
A fresh seed every launch, but a rigged console could pick its own.
Not proven yet: who claims it, when, and at what pace. That is Mumbai.
At ETHGlobal Mumbai, we'll add three networks.
World ID: your agent asks, only you approve.
Hedera: HCS seeds and checkpoints, and x402 payments.
And Arkiv: every log, on a board anyone can query.
The goal: your coach agent pays the runner just ahead of you, for their ghost.
The plan: checked on the console, published with World ID, listed on Arkiv, paid over Hedera.
PB also walks you through every sponsor step.
Real screens. The calls stay mock until Mumbai.
Don't trust the video. Check the run.
